subject.title: [OAuth] Client ID revoked `app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann` - fresh ChatGPT Plus logins completely broken

question: Should OpenClaw rotate the built-in OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex OAuth client ID now, or keep tracking upstream Codex's current client while gathering live browser-login proof?
rationale: Registering or selecting an OAuth app is an ownership and upstream-contract decision; source confirms OpenClaw still sends the reported ID, but live proof here did not confirm browser revocation and upstream Codex still uses the same ID.

options.title: Live-prove then coordinate rotation
options.body: Verify the failure with a real fresh ChatGPT Plus/Pro browser login, then rotate to an official client or approved override with coverage for browser, device-code, refresh, and account metadata paths.

options.title: Keep upstream client pending confirmation
options.body: Leave the current client ID in place until OpenAI/Codex confirms revocation or provides a replacement, while documenting API-key or other supported fallback guidance.

options.title: Add an explicit override path
options.body: Keep the built-in ID as default but add a maintainer-approved override for affected environments, accepting the extra config and support burden.

recommendation.title: Live-prove then coordinate rotation
recommendation.body: Verify the failure with a real fresh ChatGPT Plus/Pro browser login, then rotate to an official client or approved override with coverage for browser, device-code, refresh, and account metadata paths.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged OpenAI provider-unification PR and current OpenAI plugin OAuth files, so they are the strongest routing candidate for the product/upstream decision.
